Un'opacità che riempie il lobo superiore: An opacity that fills the right upper lobe and stops with a sharp horizontal margin is bounded by the horizontal fissure. There are three main causes: consolidation (pneumonia: volume preserved, air bronchogram), atelectasis (volume loss: fissure moves up, hilum and trachea pulled upwards and to the right) and mass. A hilar mass obstructing the bronchus causes atelectasis with an «S»-shaped margin (Golden sign): the picture not to miss in an elderly smoker. That is why an upper lobe opacity at this age is studied with contrast-enhanced CT; if it is treated as pneumonia, a follow-up X-ray after 6-8 weeks is mandatory, because a «pneumonia that does not resolve» may hide a tumour.
Opacità lobare nell'anziano: cerca perdi: Lobar opacity in the elderly: look for volume loss and a hilar mass; then CT, or a mandatory follow-up after antibiotics.
Opacità del campo polmonare superiore de: Opacity of the right upper lung zone with a sharp, horizontal lower margin (along the horizontal fissure)
